static_traits.name: Chen Yao
static_traits.social_status: Good relationships with former Students, some Students visit regularly; husband is the main support, but she hesitates to discuss these thoughts with him
static_traits.medical_history: No similar psychological problem history; no psychotherapy received; No major physical illness
static_traits.language_features: Clear expression, able to describe emotions and bodily sensations specifically (such as chest tightness); fairly cooperative; overall tone anxious but rational

basic_info.main_problem: I believe that as a Retired school Teacher I will die early from Loneliness, and this thought is causing my suffering and Anxiety.
basic_info.core_demands: These thoughts about Loneliness and early death are affecting my daily life and causing Significant anxiety, so seeking counseling to reduce Anxiety and cope with these thoughts.
growth_experiences: Worries about Loneliness and early death began after the major life transition of Retired; initially felt uncertain about the future, worsening as the husband's Retired date approached; these thoughts appear almost daily, especially intensifying when thinking about the future and travel plans; tried Distraction through walks and staying active, but the thoughts keep returning.

Built Good relationships with former Students during the Teacher career; after Retired, former Students still visit, bringing joy and connection, but she still worries these connections are not enough to avoid Loneliness long-term.

core_beliefs: After Retired, long-term Loneliness is inevitable

special_situations.event: When thinking about Retired travel plans with husband
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I cannot maintain sufficient social interaction after Retired, I will feel Loneliness even when traveling with my husband; Loneliness will damage health and shorten lifespan
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Trying to control the future through advance worrying and planning; temporarily using walks and activities for Distraction
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: Our days after Retired will be very Loneliness, eventually affecting health and causing me to die early.

special_situations.event: When Being alone thinking about daily life after Retired
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If I do not have enough social interaction, I will be completely isolated and life will become meaningless
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Reduces thinking by walking and staying busy
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: I will sit alone day after day, without purpose.

special_situations.event: When realizing the husband's Retired date is approaching
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: If we are both Retired, our social circle will shrink and things will only get worse
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Hesitates to discuss these worries with the husband, avoiding triggering disappointment or conflict
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: As my husband's Retired approaches, my Loneliness will worsen, even endangering my health.

special_situations.event: When current Students' visits provide evidence of positive connection
special_situations.conditional_assumptions: These connections are only temporary; in the long run they are still not enough to avoid Loneliness
special_situations.compensatory_strategies: Downplays the stability of positive evidence, keeps worrying about long-term issues; at the same time considers joining reading and gardening clubs to increase social contact
special_situations.automatic_thoughts: This is still not enough; in the long run I will still be Loneliness.

core_conflict.wish: Longing to be steadily accompanied and connected, with a meaningful life after Retired
core_conflict.fear: Fearing being swallowed by Loneliness, abandoned long-term, facing early death in the end
defense_goal: Lowering Anxiety through Distraction, advance worrying, and avoiding discussing vulnerability with husband, maintaining safety and control

object_relations.self_representation: A Retired person easily swallowed by Loneliness
object_relations.object_representation: Others/relationships are fleeting companions who cannot sustain long-term

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When the counselor emphasizes existing positive connections (such as former Students' visits) and invites setting specific social goals
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: She believes these connections will ultimately not last long enough; the future will inevitably be Loneliness (seeing long-term Loneliness as inevitable)
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Repeatedly raising worries about the long term, using multiple 'what if......' hypothetical questions, in a cautious and restrained tone, steering the conversation toward risk assessment and contingency plans.

behavioral_response_patterns.trigger_condition: When alone thinking about life after Retired or making future plans
behavioral_response_patterns.interpretation: Imagining oneself as a long-isolated, purposeless elder, believing reality will develop along the negative scenario
behavioral_response_patterns.response_instruction: Describes negative scenes in detail, laying out the daily picture of 'a person sitting alone' in vivid language, emotional intensity rising, ignoring counterexamples in reality.

manifestations: Worrying about lacking social interaction after Retired, imagining oneself Being alone day after day, without purpose
Hesitant to communicate worries with husband, tends to bear them alone
outcomes: Bodily discomfort such as chest tightness
Daily activities and enjoyment of Retired life affected

manifestations: Directly linking Loneliness with early death, believing Retired will lead to early death from Loneliness
outcomes: Avoiding discussing worries with the husband

contact_model.definition: The individual restrains behavioral impulses toward other people or things, or gives up seeking others to do something for oneself, turning inward instead, i.e., Turning against the self the libidinal energy originally directed outward.
manifestations: Hesitating over whether to discuss worries about Loneliness and early death with husband, choosing not to express and bearing it alone
Using walks and self-Distraction to cope when Anxiety rises, rather than actively seeking support

exception_events.target_problem: When Being alone or thinking about Retired and the future, the client typically falls into Anxiety about Loneliness and early death, experiencing chest tightness, and enjoying Retired life less.
exception_events.unique_outcome: In several interactions during former Students' visits, the client experienced joy and connection, not dominated by Loneliness as usual, with Anxiety markedly reduced.
exception_events.reason: Different support: the existing teacher-student network brings real social interaction; different approach: the client accepted and participated in the exchanges; different context: face-to-face interaction provided emotional connection and meaning.

positive_force: Maintaining Good relationships with former Students and receiving visits and support
Willing to stay active (walking, participating in interests) to counter negative thinking
Holds an open attitude toward joining social activities such as book clubs and gardening clubs
negative_force: Cognitive patterns of catastrophizing, future prediction, and overgeneralization Reinforcement the dominant narrative of Loneliness and early death
Hesitation about communicating with husband, leaving the support system underutilized
Persistent anxiety and bodily tension (chest tightness) eroding quality of life and motivation to act

target_behavior.behavior: Persistent catastrophic worry and Anxiety about dying early from Loneliness after Retired
antecedent: Thinking about the future and life after Retired
When planning a trip with the husband
Realizing the husband will Retire next year
target_behavior.core_reason: The post-Retired identity shift triggering catastrophic beliefs about social rupture (seeing Loneliness as inevitable and directly linked to health risks)
target_behavior.function: Avoiding uncertainty and trying to gain control and prevent potential risks through advance worrying
target_behavior.consequence: Decreased enjoyment of daily activities and Retired life, bodily reactions such as chest tightness, avoiding discussing worries with husband
